page.title: Storage Manager
page.description: See which folders take the most space on a DGX Spark, check what Docker is holding on to, and delete what you no longer need.
page.noSpark: No DGX Spark to look at
page.noSparkHelp: Storage Manager works with DGX Spark units. Add one from the sidebar and it will show up here.
page.offlineHelp: Analysing, deleting and Docker work again once it can be reached.
page.readingHelp: Checking the disks and what this account is allowed to do.
page.dockerOffline: Docker on {{name}} cannot be read while it is offline
page.dockerOfflineHelp: Docker’s images and containers are read live from the Spark. Nothing about them is saved here.
page.accessNotice: Who can do this: everyone who can open this dashboard can analyse, delete and use a remembered sudo password on every Spark listed here. There are no separate accounts, and Activity records what was done, not who did it.
page.noSavedAnalysis: There is no saved analysis for it yet.
page.savedJustNow: You are looking at the analysis saved just now.
page.savedEarlier: You are looking at the analysis saved {{age}} ago.

disk.almostFull: This disk is almost full. Models may fail to download or load until some space is freed.
disk.containerAccount: Runs via the dashboard's container as {{account}}
disk.containerHelp: The dashboard runs in a container and enters the Spark's file system from there, so the account, home folder and environment are the container's.
disk.localHelp: The dashboard runs directly on this Spark and starts the commands itself.
disk.sshHelp: Commands run over SSH as the account set for this Spark.

files.previousReadError: Could not read the earlier analysis: {{error}}
files.offlineNoAnalysis: Analyse {{sparkName}} once it can be reached again; the result is kept here for when it is offline.
files.hardLinkedStays: {{shared}} of it is hard-linked elsewhere and stays on disk until its other links are deleted.
files.scanBlocksDelete: A scan is using this Spark: nothing can be deleted until it has finished.
files.bulkDeleteRunning: A bulk delete is still running on this Spark.
files.offlineFolder: The saved analysis did not measure inside this folder. It can be looked inside once {{sparkName}} can be reached again.
files.unmeasuredFolder: This folder has not been measured yet.
files.incompleteSizes: , so the sizes below are incomplete{{uncounted}}. Docker’s storage is usually one of them.
files.uncountedSpace: (about {{bytes}} of the used space is not counted)
files.timedOut: The Spark stopped this analysis early because it was taking very long, so sizes are incomplete. Try a smaller folder.
files.bulkDeleteHold: A bulk delete started earlier is still running. The Spark stays busy until it has finished.
files.unusualName: The name has unusual characters, so it cannot be deleted from here.
files.includedInSelection: Included: it is inside {{name}}, which is selected.
files.deleteLocked: {{reason}}: nothing can be deleted until it is back.
files.dateBefore1980: Not known: the date recorded for it is before 1980, which means it was never really set.
files.dateUnreadable: Not known: no date could be read for it, or the scan that measured it did not record one.
files.datesNotRecorded: Not known: this analysis did not record dates.
files.sharedBytesTitle: {{bytes}} of this is hard-linked to files outside it, so it stays on disk when this is deleted.
files.allBytesFreed: Deleting this gives back all of its size.
files.deleteNoSpaceTitle: Delete {{name}}. Deleting frees no space: everything in it is also linked from elsewhere.
files.analysedStale: . Sizes may have changed since: analyse again to refresh.
files.analyseLocked: {{reason}}: it cannot be analysed until it is back
files.basicScanNote: Basic scan: a file hard-linked into several folders may be counted in each of them here.
files.basicScanNoDates: It does not record when things last changed.
files.oldAnalysisNoDates: This analysis was made before dates were recorded: analyse again to see when things last changed.
files.sharedNote: Hatched parts are shared: hard-linked to files outside that folder, so deleting the folder does not free them. Frees counts only what would really come back.
files.overlapNote: Some folders here hold links to the same files, so their sizes add up to more than the folder.
files.newestSortTitle: Sorted by last change, newest first. Click for oldest first.
files.oldestSortTitle: Sorted by last change, oldest first. Click for newest first.
files.dateSortTitle: Sort by when anything inside last changed
files.nothingDeletable: Nothing shown here can be deleted from the dashboard
files.name: Name
files.lastChangedTitle: When anything inside it was last modified
files.freesTitle: Bytes that come back if you delete it. Files that are also hard-linked from outside stay.
files.onlyTinyItems: It only holds a few tiny items.

folders.empty: No folders inside. Analyse this folder, or go up.
folders.more: Only the first folders are shown. Open a parent folder to narrow it down.

analyse.title: What should I look at on {{sparkName}}?
analyse.description: Analyse measures every folder and file below the place you pick and lists the biggest first. It only reads, nothing is changed or deleted until you choose to.

disk.title: Whole disk
disk.hint: Everything on the main drive. The best place to start.

home.title: Home folder
home.hint: Your own files: models, datasets, projects.

cache.title: Cache folder
cache.hint: Caches that programs keep. Often large, and rebuilt when needed.

custom.title: A specific folder
custom.hint: Click through the folders on the Spark and pick one.

analyse.includeProtected: Include folders only administrators can open
analyse.includeProtectedHint: Recommended. Without it, protected folders such as Docker’s storage are not counted and the totals come up short.
analyse.insecureSudoNotice: This Spark asks for a sudo password and this connection is not private, so it cannot be typed here. Open the dashboard over https or from the Spark itself, or turn on Settings → Allow sudo password over plain http, to include protected folders.

scan.stopAdminNote: This scan runs as administrator, so the dashboard cannot stop it. It will stop by itself{{suffix}}.
scan.stopUnconfirmed: Could not confirm it stopped — the Spark stays busy until it does.
scan.stopBestEffort: Stopping is best effort here: the dashboard runs in a container and may not see every process of the scan.
scan.stopUnconfirmedHold: Could not confirm the scan stopped — the Spark stays busy until it does.
scan.stoppingHold: The scan on this Spark is being stopped. Other storage work waits until it has.
scan.runningHold: A scan is still running on this Spark{{suffix}}.
scan.lostContactHold: The dashboard lost contact with this Spark during the last scan, so the Spark stays busy until the dashboard can confirm the scan has ended{{suffix}}.
scan.adminCannotStop: Scans run as administrator cannot be stopped from the dashboard
scan.stopBestEffortTitle: Stopping is best effort while the dashboard runs in a container
scan.progressDescription: Measuring every folder on {{sparkName}}. A whole disk usually takes under a minute (longer the first time, while the disk is cold). The scan runs at low priority, so models and other work on the Spark keep running normally.
scan.noProcessLeft: Nothing of it is left running on the Spark.

deletion.noTrash: There is no trash to restore from.
deletion.adminHint: Needed for files that belong to root or another account, such as Docker's.
deletion.manual: Or run this in a terminal on the Spark
deletion.badPassword: The sudo password was not accepted. Check it and try again.
deletion.ackRequired: Deleting folders as administrator is off for this Spark. Read the note below and confirm it to go on.
deletion.sharedNone: Deleting this will not free any space.
deletion.sharedDetail: {{shared}} is hard-linked to files outside {{target}}, so it stays on disk until every link is deleted. {{result}}
deletion.removeNames: Delete it only if you want to get rid of these names.
deletion.removeTheseNames: Delete them only if you want to get rid of these names.
deletion.continues: The Spark deletes them one at a time. It keeps going if you close or reload this page.
deletion.included_one: {{count}} item inside selected folders is included
deletion.included_other: {{count}} items inside selected folders are included

advice.looking: Looking on {{sparkName}} for programs and containers using {{target}}, recent changes, partial downloads, keys and logins, and git work.
advice.checkFailed: The check could not be done: {{message}}.
advice.skip: You chose not to wait for the check.
advice.proceedCarefully: Nothing about {{target}} was checked, so proceed with care.
advice.checked: Checked on {{sparkName}}: programs and running containers using {{target}}, recent changes, partial downloads, files that look like keys or logins, git work, and SparkDash's own launchers and LLM servers.
advice.checkItems: Items the check has something to say about
advice.readStillDelete: I have read this and still want to delete {{target}}.
advice.typePhrase: Type {{phrase}} to delete {{target}} all the same

recovery.title: Needs attention
recovery.intro_one: A delete on {{sparkName}} did not finish. What was moved aside is kept until you put it back or delete it.
recovery.intro_other: {{count}} deletes on {{sparkName}} did not finish. What was moved aside is kept until you put it back or delete it.
recovery.recordOnly: Only the dashboard's record of the unfinished delete is removed. Nothing on the Spark changes.
recovery.restoreHint: It goes back to {{path}}. If something new has that name now, nothing is replaced and it stays here.

state.staged: A delete moved it aside and did not finish. It still takes space.
state.interrupted: Its delete stopped part way, so some of it may already be gone.
state.conflict: It could not be put back because something new has its name.
state.inPlace: The delete stopped before anything moved. It is still in its place.
state.gone: It is no longer there. Only the record of the unfinished delete is left.
state.unknown: Something else is where it was kept. Check {{path}} on the Spark by hand.
state.unreadable: The record of this delete cannot be read. Check {{path}} on the Spark by hand.

recovery.deleteWarning: {{target}} deleted from the Spark’s disk, after the same safety checks as any delete.
recovery.folderAndContents: The folder and everything in it are

admin.ackTitle: Deleting folders as administrator is off for this Spark.
admin.ackText: Administrator deletion can remove folders that the dashboard account cannot normally change. It runs the delete as {{account}} with administrator rights. Only enable it if processes running as {{account}} are trusted.
admin.ackConfirm: I understand. Allow administrator deletes of folders on this Spark.
admin.alreadyRoot: The dashboard already runs as an administrator on this Spark. No password is needed.
admin.passwordless: This Spark allows administrator actions without a password. No password is needed.
admin.saved: The sudo password for this Spark is remembered on the dashboard (encrypted), so nothing needs typing. Anyone who can open the dashboard can use it until it is forgotten.
admin.rememberHint: Kept encrypted on the dashboard server, so you are not asked again, even after a reload. Anyone who can open this dashboard can then use it on this Spark.
admin.cannotType: This Spark asks for a sudo password, and this connection is not private (plain http from another machine), so it cannot be typed here. Open the dashboard over https or from the Spark itself, turn on Settings → Allow sudo password over plain http (only on a network you trust), or run the command in a terminal on the Spark.

builtHere.title: No registry digest is recorded for this image: it was built or loaded on this Spark, not pulled. Removing it may delete the only copy; it would have to be built again.
builtHere.label: Built here, not pulled

peers.title: Also on your other Sparks
peers.unusedAdmin: None is used there (removed as administrator).
peers.inUse: Used by containers there, so it would be kept.
peers.partlyUsed: {{unused}} unused will go; {{used}} used are kept.
peers.keptAll: {{spark}}: every copy is in use there, so none were removed.

docker.readingHint: Docker measures its images and layers, which can take a few seconds.
docker.containersUnknown: Docker did not list its containers, so whether an image is in use is unknown and nothing is offered for removal.
docker.imagesUnknown: Some images could not be read, so this list may be incomplete.
docker.imagesUnlisted: The images could not be listed.
docker.noImages: There are no images on this Spark.
docker.sizeFootnote: Sizes use 1 GB = 1024 MB like the rest of sparkDash, so they read about 7% lower than the Docker command line, which counts in thousands. Images share layers, so the sizes listed overlap: they add up to far more than the space the images really use.
docker.noStopped: Every container is running. Nothing to clean up here.
docker.noRemovalUnknown: Which containers use these images could not be checked, so none of them can be removed right now.
docker.noUnused: Every image is used by a container. Nothing to clean up here.
docker.adminTitle: Docker commands run through sudo on this Spark
docker.usedImageTitle_one: {{usedBy}}. Remove the container first (button on the right).
docker.usedImageTitle_other: {{usedBy}}. Remove the containers first (button on the right).
docker.stoppedSummary_one: {{count}} stopped container. It keeps its image on disk, which is why that image cannot be removed. Removing a container keeps its volumes but deletes its writable layer, which may hold data you can’t re-create.
docker.stoppedSummary_other: {{count}} stopped containers. They keep their images on disk, which is why those images cannot be removed. Removing a container keeps its volumes but deletes its writable layer, which may hold data you can’t re-create.
docker.unusedSummary_one: {{count}} unused image: no container uses it.
docker.unusedSummary_other: {{count}} unused images: no container uses them.
docker.reclaimSummary: Docker estimates that removing all unused images frees about {{size}}.
docker.reviewBeforeRemove: Review before removing: a pulled image can only be pulled again while its registry still has it.
docker.builtSummary_one: Of these, one was built here, not pulled, so it may be the only copy.
docker.builtSummary_other: Of these, {{count}} were built here, not pulled, so they may be the only copies.
docker.sharedSpace: less than their combined {{size}}, because images share layers
docker.imagesHint: Downloaded or built images. Unused ones can be removed below.
docker.containersHint: Running and stopped containers, with the files they wrote.
docker.volumesHint: Data kept for containers. Not touched here.
docker.buildCacheHint: Layers kept to speed up builds. Clear it with docker builder prune.
docker.rootNote: Docker keeps all of this in {{path}}. It shows up there on the Files tab when you analyse with administrator access.
docker.imagesKept: The images are still used by other containers, so they were kept.
docker.containersRemovedImagesFailed: The containers are gone, but the images could not be removed: {{error}}.
docker.imagesSkipped_one: {{count}} skipped because a container started using it.
docker.imagesSkipped_other: {{count}} skipped because a container started using them.

quickCleanup.title: Quick clean-up
quickCleanup.description: Get Docker space back in a click or two. Each button first shows exactly what would go; nothing is removed until you confirm.
quickCleanup.problems: What was kept or could not be removed
quickCleanup.nothingRecommended: Nothing to clean with the recommended rules right now.
quickCleanup.volumesTitle: Volumes are never cleaned from here:
quickCleanup.volumesText: they can hold data, such as databases or downloaded models, that exists nowhere else, and Docker cannot tell whether something outside a container still needs it.
quickCleanup.sheetLead: Only what is listed below goes from {{spark}}. The Spark checks each item again right before removing it and skips anything that changed. Running containers, volumes and your files are never touched.
quickCleanup.includeBuilt: Also include {{count}} images built on this Spark
quickCleanup.includeBuiltHint: No registry copy is recorded for these images, so they may not be re-creatable: removing one may delete the only copy. Left out unless ticked.
quickCleanup.peersHint: Each Spark is checked with the same rule on its own list. Tick the ones to clean up too; build cache is cleared on {{spark}} only.

removeImages.badPassword: The sudo password was not accepted. Check it and try again.
removeImages.changed: If an image gets a container before this runs, it is skipped.
removeImages.peersHint: Clusters usually keep the same images on every node. Tick the Sparks to clean up too.
removeImages.lead_one: No container uses this image. Removing it frees {{estimate}}. A pulled image comes back only by pulling it again, while its registry still has it; one built here has to be built again. Containers, volumes and your files are not touched.
removeImages.lead_other: No container uses these images. Removing them frees {{estimate}}. A pulled image comes back only by pulling it again, while its registry still has it; one built here has to be built again. Containers, volumes and your files are not touched.
removeImages.builtWarning_one: {{count}} of them was built here, not pulled: removing it may delete the only copy.
removeImages.builtWarning_other: {{count}} of them were built here, not pulled: removing them may delete the only copies.
removeImages.allBuiltWarning_one: It was built here, not pulled: removing it may delete the only copy.
removeImages.allBuiltWarning_other: All were built here, not pulled: removing them may delete the only copies.

removeContainers.badPassword: The sudo password was not accepted. Check it and try again.
removeContainers.leadOne: This container is stopped. Removing it deletes its writable layer: everything written inside it that is not in a volume. That may hold data you can’t re-create. Volumes and the images are kept, and a container that started running again is skipped.
removeContainers.leadOther: These containers are stopped. Removing them deletes their writable layers: everything written inside them that is not in a volume. That may hold data you can’t re-create. Volumes and the images are kept, and a container that started running again is skipped.
removeContainers.alsoImagesHint: This is what frees the disk space. An image another container still uses is kept.
removeContainers.alsoImages_one: Also remove the image it used, if nothing else uses it
removeContainers.alsoImages_other: Also remove the {{count}} images they used, if nothing else uses them
removeContainers.builtWarning_one: It was built here, not pulled: removing it may delete the only copy.
removeContainers.builtWarning_other: Some were built here, not pulled: removing them may delete the only copies.

quickDetails.usageUnknown: Usage unknown: docker did not list its containers, so what is in use is unknown
quickDetails.oldImagesTitle: Unused images created more than {{days}} ago
quickDetails.oldImagesDescription: No container uses them, not even a stopped one. Docker keeps no last-used date for images, so their age is when they were created.
quickDetails.danglingImagesDescription: Untagged images (<none>), usually left behind when a tag is built or pulled again. No container uses them.
quickDetails.unusedImagesDescription: Every image no container uses, whatever its age.
quickDetails.oldContainersTitle: Stopped containers that exited more than {{days}} ago
quickDetails.oldContainersDescription: Removing one deletes its writable layer: anything written inside it that is not in a volume. Volumes are kept.
quickDetails.buildCacheTitle: Build cache not used in the last {{days}}
quickDetails.buildCacheDescription: Layers Docker keeps to speed up builds. Docker removes only cache no build is using; the next build may take longer.
quickDetails.recommendedNote: Unused images and stopped containers older than {{days}}, and build cache not used in that time: {{items}}.
quickDetails.untick: You can untick any of it.
quickDetails.couldNotConfirmStopped: Docker could not confirm it is stopped
quickDetails.couldNotConfirmUnused: Docker could not confirm nothing uses it
quickDetails.cacheStepFailed: build cache could not be cleaned ({{message}})
quickDetails.keptSummary_one: {{count}} item was kept or could not be removed (listed below).
quickDetails.keptSummary_other: {{count}} items were kept or could not be removed (listed below).
quickDetails.spaceUnchanged: Available space on {{mount}} did not change while this ran.
quickDetails.spaceChanged: Available space on {{mount}} changed by {{change}} while this ran.
quickDetails.peerUnknown: Docker did not list its containers, so what is in use is unknown there.
quickDetails.noPeerSelection: Nothing ticked above applies to other Sparks.
quickDetails.peerNothingToClean: Nothing to clean there with this rule
quickDetails.imagesReclaimable: Docker estimated about {{bytes}} reclaimable for the images.
quickDetails.containersReclaimable: Docker estimated about {{bytes}} reclaimable for the containers.
quickDetails.cacheReclaimed: Docker reports {{bytes}} of build cache reclaimed.
